# Human-centred controls for trustworthy AI work

[Open this section on the publisher’s website](https://cyberdudeuk.github.io/ai-capability-governance/#assurance)

The numbers in brackets identify elements in the ordered DOM inventory. This is a text projection of Em’s material.

## Human-centred controls for trustworthy AI work [19512]

[19513] Risk-based human-in-the-loop controls make sure AI never grants authority a user does not already possess, and that every material output can be defended after the fact.

## The five-stage assurance workflow [19514]

[19516] Classify — identify service impact, data sensitivity, equality and accessibility risk, security risk and model/agent autonomy. Use the triage tool →

[19519] Select — apply the standards, source guidance, skills, agents, conformance packs and review level the classification demands.

[19521] Execute — work with least privilege, mandatory source citation, deterministic checks and pair or buddy support where competence is thin.

[19523] Review — 4-eyes or 6-eyes review, specialist assurance, and no self-approval for material or high-risk outputs.

[19525] Learn — capture evidence, incidents, near-misses, feedback, source drift and model changes; feed them back into the corpus.

## The H0–H5 human review model [19527]

[19530] Review levels, when they apply and the evidence each produces

[19533] Level

[19534] Name

[19535] What it means

[19536] Typical examples

[19537] Evidence

[19540] H0

[19542] No review needed

[19544] Personal, throwaway, non-published exploration with no personal or sensitive data.

[19545] Explaining a concept to yourself; drafting private notes.

[19546] None required.

[19548] H1

[19550] Self-check

[19552] Author verifies facts, sources and accessibility before use. Low impact, easily reversible.

[19553] Internal meeting notes, first-draft ideas.

[19554] AI-use note in the document.

[19556] H2

[19558] Peer check

[19560] A second competent person checks output before it leaves the team.

[19561] Internal reports, non-public analysis, low-risk code in a sandbox.

[19562] Reviewer name, date, issues found.

[19564] H3

[19566] Specialist review (4-eyes)

[19568] A named specialist in the relevant discipline reviews. No self-approval.

[19569] Accessibility, security, legal, statistical or clinical content; production code.

[19570] Specialist sign-off + test results.

[19572] H4

[19574] Multi-specialist review (6-eyes)

[19576] Two or more specialisms plus the accountable owner. Independent challenge required.

[19577] Public-facing decisions, casework support, anything affecting entitlements.

[19578] Panel record, dissent captured, residual risk stated.

[19580] H5

[19582] Governance board and publication

[19584] Formal board approval, published transparency record and monitored deployment.

[19585] Automated or semi-automated decisions about people; national services.

[19586] ATRS record, DPIA, EQIA, monitoring plan, review date.

## Reviewer checklist [19587]

## Always check [19590]

[19592] Every citation opens, exists and says what the text claims

[19593] Numbers, dates, thresholds and legal references independently verified

[19594] Nothing asserts compliance that has not actually been tested

[19595] No personal or sensitive data was entered into an unapproved tool

[19596] Accessibility and plain-language requirements met, not assumed

[19597] Assumptions, gaps and residual risk stated explicitly

[19598] Reviewer is independent of the author at H3 and above

## Common failure patterns [19600]

[19602] • Confident fabrication — plausible citations that do not exist

[19604] • Stale authority — quoting withdrawn or superseded guidance

[19606] • Compliance theatre — a checklist ticked without a test run

[19608] • Silent scope creep — an agent doing more than was authorised

[19610] • Automation bias — reviewers rubber-stamping fluent output

[19612] • Averaged users — outputs tuned to a majority that excludes minorities

[19614] • Evidence gaps — no record of who checked what, or when

## Accountability at a glance (RACI) [19616]

[19619] Who does what in AI-assisted delivery

[19623] Responsible

[19626] Informed

[19636] Author

# Treat skills, agents and code as assets in their own right

[Open this section on the publisher’s website](https://cyberdudeuk.github.io/ai-capability-governance/#catalogue)

The numbers in brackets identify elements in the ordered DOM inventory. This is a text projection of Em’s material.

## Treat skills, agents and code as assets in their own right [19673]

[19674] Every reusable AI capability should be discoverable, accountable, interoperable and governed like any other public asset — with an owner, a version, a risk rating and a retirement plan.

## Catalogue fields [19677]

[19680] Minimum viable metadata for any AI asset

[19683] Field

[19684] Why it matters

[19687] asset_id

[19689] Stable identifier so evidence, incidents and dependencies can point at it.

[19691] owner

[19693] A named person, not a team inbox. Accountability needs a face.

[19695] status

[19697] draft / approved / restricted / deprecated / withdrawn.

[19699] version

[19701] Semantic versioning; breaking changes force re-review.

[19703] authority_tier

[19705] 0–3 tier of the sources the asset relies on.

[19707] risk_level / human_review

[19710] H0–H5 floor that consumers must apply.

[19712] source_provenance

[19714] Which guidance, data and code it derives from, with dates.

[19716] permissions

[19718] Least-privilege scopes, tools and credentials the asset may use.

[19720] prohibited_actions

[19722] Explicit red lines an agent must never cross.

[19724] deia_screen

[19726] Date and outcome of equality and accessibility screening.

[19728] evaluation

[19730] Test suite, pass thresholds and last run.

[19732] compatibility

[19734] Models, runtimes and versions it is validated against.

[19736] lifecycle

[19738] Review cadence, next review, deprecation and retirement date.

[19740] contact / redress

[19743] How to report a problem or challenge an outcome.

## Example skill asset metadata [19745]

[19747] Copy

[19748] asset_type: ai_skill asset_id: review-accessibility-govuk title: GOV.UK accessibility review assistant status: approved version: 2.1.0 owner: AI assurance lead (role, not a named person) authority_tier: 1 human_review: H3 specialist_review: [accessibility, content_design] self_approval: false source_provenance:   - id: wcag22     url: https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/     checked: 2026-07-14     next_check: 2026-10-14   - id: govuk-design-system     url: https://design-system.service.gov.uk/     checked: 2026-07-14 permissions:   tools: [read_page, run_axe]   data_classification_max: OFFICIAL prohibited_actions:   - claiming_conformance_without_test_evidence   - processing_personal_data   - autonomous_publication deia_screen:   completed: 2026-06-02   outcome: mitigations_applied evaluation:   suite: a11y-regression-v4   threshold: 0.95   last_run: 2026-08-01 compatibility:   models: [">=v3.1"]   runtimes: [node20, python3.12] evidence_rules:   require_citations: true   require_reviewer_signoff: true   retain_for: P7Y lifecycle:   review_cadence: P3M   next_review: 2026-11-01   deprecation: null contact: https://github.com/cyberdudeuk/ai-capability-governance/issues/new

[19750] Interoperability note: map these fields to DCAT 3 (opens an external website) for cataloguing, PROV-O (opens an external website) for evidence chains and CycloneDX ML-BOM (opens an external website) for supply chain, so registries in different organisations can federate rather than fork.

# Tell us what is wrong, missing or unclear

[Open this section on the publisher’s website](https://cyberdudeuk.github.io/ai-capability-governance/#contact)

The numbers in brackets identify elements in the ordered DOM inventory. This is a text projection of Em’s material.

## Tell us what is wrong, missing or unclear [22178]

[22179] Every route below goes through GitHub, so it is public and auditable. There is no email route. Choose the one that fits — if you are not sure, raise an issue and we will redirect it.

## Something is broken [22183]

[22184] Broken links, tools that do not work, layout failures, incorrect calculations or console errors.

[22185] Report a bug on GitHub

## An accessibility barrier [22189]

[22190] Anything that stops you using this site with a screen reader, keyboard, magnification, voice control or any other assistive technology. These are treated as priority defects.

[22191] Report a barrier

[22193] Target first response: 5 working days.

## A feature or resource request [22196]

[22197] A tool you need, a section that is missing, or an authoritative source that should be in the library.

[22198] Request a feature

## Content is wrong or out of date [22202]

[22203] Superseded guidance, a withdrawn standard, a mis-stated legal duty or a dead authority link. Include the source that proves it.

[22204] Submit a correction

## A security vulnerability [22208]

[22209] Do not open a public issue. Use private disclosure so we can fix it before it is known. See our security policy for scope and timescales.

[22210] Report privately

## A question or an idea [22214]

[22215] Not sure it is a defect? Want to talk about approach, reuse this in your organisation, or contribute? Start there.

[22216] Use the contact form

## Write it here first [22218]

[22219] This form helps you write a clear report, then opens the GitHub contact form with it filled in. Issues are public: do not include personal data, case details or anything above OFFICIAL. For a security problem, use private reporting instead.

[22223] Your name (optional)

[22227] Organisation (optional)

[22231] What is this about?

[22233] General enquiry

[22234] Accessibility barrier

[22235] Content correction

[22236] Feature or resource suggestion

[22237] Reuse or adaptation in my organisation

[22238] Partnership or contribution

[22239] Data protection or privacy question

[22240] Something else

[22242] Subject

[22245] Which page or section does this concern? (optional)

[22249] Your message

[22253] Assistive technology you were using (optional, helps us reproduce accessibility issues)

[22258] I understand GitHub issues are public and I have not included personal or sensitive information.

[22260] Open the contact form on GitHub

[22261] Copy message instead

[22262] Clear form

[22264] A preview of your message will appear here before anything is sent.

## What happens to your message [22265]

## How it is handled [22268]

[22270] • Nothing is transmitted from this page. The form builds a report and opens GitHub with it, so you stay in control of what is posted.

[22271] • GitHub issues are public. Do not put personal or sensitive information in them.

[22272] • Accessibility reports are logged as defects with a target first response of five working days.

[22273] • Security reports follow coordinated disclosure and are never opened as public issues.

## If we cannot resolve it [22275]

[22277] • Ask for the decision to be reviewed by the accountable owner named in the transparency section.

[22278] • For accessibility complaints in the UK, you can escalate to the Equality Advisory and Support Service .

[22280] • For data protection concerns, contact the host organisation's data protection officer, then the Information Commissioner's Office .

[22282] • All correspondence about this repository is capable of being disclosed under freedom of information law.

# Glossary and frequently asked questions

[Open this section on the publisher’s website](https://cyberdudeuk.github.io/ai-capability-governance/#glossary)

The numbers in brackets identify elements in the ordered DOM inventory. This is a text projection of Em’s material.

## Glossary and frequently asked questions [21433]

## Glossary [21436]

[21438] Filter terms

[21442] 4-eyes / 6-eyes

[21443] Two or three independent people involved in producing and approving an output.

[21445] accept

[21446] Used as produced, with no material change.

[21448] Agent

[21449] Software that plans and acts across multiple steps using tools, within explicit permissions and bounds.

[21451] Agent register

[21452] An operational inventory of deployed agents with named owners, approved sources, autonomy tier and retirement trigger.

[21454] Agent sprawl / orphaned agents

[21455] Agents outlive purpose, owner or service; estate accumulates unowned automation.

[21457] Agent washing

[21458] Rebranding existing automation as agentic; Gartner assesses ~130 of thousands of vendors as genuine.

[21460] Agentic

[21461] A capability that takes actions across tools under delegated authority, choosing its own path to a goal.

[21463] alb

[21464] Arm's-length body, agency or public corporation.

[21466] analyst

[21467] Produces analysis rather than decisions.

[21469] anti_streak

[21470] The interface changed state following a run of unmodified approvals.

[21472] Approval fatigue

[21473] Volume-driven degradation of review quality — the agentic form of clinical alert fatigue Remedy: Batching, risk-triage of what reaches a human at all.

[21475] assist

[21476] Drafts, summarises or analyses. No decision about a person is attached to the output.

[21478] Assist / recommend / determine

[21479] Deployment classes: assist = drafting/summarisation, no decision; recommend = informs a decision a person makes; determine = constitutes or directly produces the decision.

[21481] Assisted digital

[21482] Support for people who cannot use a digital service independently.

[21484] Assurance tier

[21485] The proportionate level of control an agent attracts, derived from criticality rather than popularity.

[21487] ATRS

[21488] Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard — the UK format for publishing algorithmic tool use.

[21490] Authority

[21491] What an agent is permitted to do, as distinct from what it is technically capable of doing.

[21493] Automation bias

[21494] The tendency to accept an automated output without enough scrutiny.

[21496] Automation complacency

[21497] Reduced monitoring effort — not looking rather than looking and agreeing Remedy: Canaries; anti-streak interventions.

[21499] Automation drift

[21500] The gradual shift of an automated system's behaviour or use over time so it no longer aligns with the original design intent or approved scope. (Adopted from TBS Canada.)

[21502] Automation drift vs model/data/concept drift

[21503] Automation drift is behaviour or use shifting away from approved scope — a governance question. Model, data and concept drift are statistical changes in inputs or the target relationship — an ML operations question.

[21505] Autonomy level

[21506] How far an agent may act without a human decision, from suggest-only to bounded execution.

[21508] Barometer

[21509] The eight-dimension readiness self-assessment held on the reader's own device.

[21511] bias_pattern

[21512] The output reflects a disparate pattern across a protected characteristic.

[21514] Bimodality coefficient

[21515] (skew²+1)/(excess kurtosis + 3(n−1)²/((n−2)(n−3))); >~0.555 suggests bimodality; applied to time-to-decision as rubber-stamping signature.

[21517] Bounded autonomy

[21518] TBS Canada principle: tight explicit limits on data, tools, permissions and scope; labelled activity level ('draft only','read only'); named trained owners incl. sub-agents.

[21520] Canary

[21521] Synthetic known-bad output injected at low randomised rate under ethics approval with guaranteed downstream suppression.

[21523] canary.detected

[21524] True only where the reviewer's action demonstrates detection — modify, reject or escalate citing the seeded defect. Accepting a canary is never 'detected'.

[21526] Capability class

[21527] Whether a deployment is generative, agentic or declarative — the determinant of which controls carry the weight.

[21529] caseworker

[21530] Handles individual cases within established policy.

[21532] central_department

[21533] Ministerial or non-ministerial department.

[21535] Cognitive debt

[21536] Kosmyna et al. term for reduced cognitive engagement and unaided performance after LLM assistance.

[21538] Compensatory use

[21539] AI use that offsets a stable access barrier — one that's stable regardless of effort (e.g. drafting support for dyslexia, checking tone, structuring a first draft, holding several things in working memory). Carries little skill-atrophy risk because the underlying skill was never the bottleneck. 'This is what assistive technology is.'

[21541] Comprehension debt

[21542] Loss of understanding of code created via AI generation; targeted by comprehension gates at PR.

[21544] confidence_gated

[21545] The output was withheld because model uncertainty was high.

[21547] Conformance pack

[21548] A bundle of automated checks that tests an artefact against a named standard.

[21550] Connector

[21551] An integration that lets an AI tool read from, or write to, another system.

[21553] consecutive_unmodified_count

[21554] Derived from the actual ordered sequence of dispositions within a session. Reset to zero on any disposition other than 'accept'. Never estimated or sampled.

[21556] Contestability erosion

[21557] If the decision-maker cannot explain reasoning, the citizen cannot meaningfully challenge it.

[21559] Copilot Credit

[21560] The consumption billing unit for Microsoft agent activity, replacing the previous message unit from 1 September 2025.

[21562] Counterfactual

[21563] The comparison against which a benefit is measured, typically a group not using the tool.

[21565] Criticality

[21566] Operational dependency and consequence of failure, scored across ten dimensions to set the gate.

[21568] Crypto-agility

[21569] The ability to change cryptographic algorithms without redesigning the system.

[21571] Curb-cut framing / effect

[21572] Framing an accessibility tool by benefits that accrue to everyone, rather than as a deficit fix.

[21574] Currency

[21575] Recency/proficiency regime by analogy with aviation recency and clinical revalidation; NHS DCB0129/DCB0160 Clinical Safety Officer as domestic precedent.

[21577] Data boundary

[21578] A supplier commitment about where data is stored and processed. Check which features and models sit outside it.

[21580] DBT 'cold turkey' test

[21581] Imagine the licence removed tomorrow: which tasks become mildly annoying vs genuinely destabilising.

[21583] Decay class

[21584] How quickly a claim goes out of date: structural, positional, volatile or expiring.

[21586] Declarative

[21587] A capability defined by a specification — instructions, sources, permitted actions and constraints — that the platform executes.

[21589] Declarative agent

[21590] An agent defined by configuration: purpose, instructions, knowledge and permitted actions, run on a platform’s own model and orchestration.

[21592] Degraded-mode operating standard

[21593] Every agentic deployment demonstrates periodically and for real that the service runs without the agent at acceptable quality for a defined period.

[21595] DEIA

[21596] Diversity, equity, inclusion and accessibility.

[21598] Delegation competence

[21599] Skill of setting appropriate bounds, reading evidence they are wrong, and withdrawing agency without service collapse. Replaces task-audit definition of oversight competence.

[21601] Deployment route

[21602] The same model reached directly, through a cloud platform or inside another supplier’s product is a different governance object each time.

[21604] Deprecation

[21605] A supplier’s notice that a model, feature or interface will be withdrawn.

[21607] determine

[21608] The output constitutes, or directly produces, a decision about a person.

[21610] Deterministic automation

[21611] Rules-based automation that gives the same output for the same input every time.

[21613] developer

[21614] Builds or maintains the system.

[21616] Digital worker

[21617] An agent framed as a managed member of the workforce, with recruitment, probation, review and retirement.

[21619] disconfirmation_panel

[21620] Contradicting evidence was surfaced alongside the output.

[21622] DPIA

[21623] Data protection impact assessment, required for high-risk processing.

[21625] Drift

[21626] Divergence between a cited source, a model version or a control and what is actually in use.

[21628] Earned autonomy

[21629] Teams demonstrating sustained catch performance move to lighter oversight modes and higher agent autonomy.

[21631] Easy Read

[21632] Accessible format: short sentences, one idea per chunk, large type, simple icon per point, plain words, explicit permission to ignore what doesn't fit; normally reviewed by Easy Read readers before publication.

[21634] edit_distance_normalised

[21635] Normalised difference between the output as presented and the output as finalised, in [0,1]. Report the algorithm used alongside the data; values are not comparable across different distance measures.

[21637] EQIA

[21638] Equality impact assessment evidencing the public sector equality duty.

[21640] equality_concern

[21641] The output raised a potential discriminatory or disparate-impact issue.

[21643] escalate

[21644] Referred to another person or process rather than decided.

[21646] Evidence card

[21647] The standard record of a claim: what was done, method, result, publisher, date and known limitations.

[21649] Evidence log

[21650] A record of how a piece of AI-assisted work was produced, retained with the work.

[21652] Evidence pack

[21653] The bundle of records proving how an AI-assisted output was produced, checked and approved.

[21655] Exit path

[21656] The seven-step route out of a platform, model or supplier dependency: discover, target, design, extract, test, cutover, decommission.

[21658] Expiring

[21659] Carries an explicit date. Auto-flags for review on that date.

[21661] extension

[21662] Local codes must be namespaced with a 'x_' prefix (e.g. 'x_local_triage_override'). Anything unprefixed is reserved for the central vocabulary so that local extension never collides with a future addition.

[21664] FACT / INTERPRETATION convention

[21665] Evidence-discipline convention used in turn-5 paragraph.

[21667] factual_correction

[21668] A fact in the output was wrong.

[21670] factual_error

[21671] A verifiably incorrect fact.

[21673] FASTER principles

[21674] Canada: Fair, Accountable, Secure, Transparent, Educated, Relevant.

[21676] FinOps

[21677] The practice of joining consumption, cost, quality and value so spend is forecast, allocated and optimised.

[21679] Friction budget

[21680] f(consequence of error × model uncertainty × recency of demonstrated catch performance × novelty of the case).

[21682] Generative

[21683] A capability that produces content, analysis or options; nothing changes until a person acts on the output.

[21685] Grounding

[21686] Supplying authoritative source material so outputs can be traced, cited and checked.

[21688] Guardrail

[21689] A constraint that holds regardless of instruction: prohibited actions, data limits, escalation triggers.

[21691] Harvest now, decrypt later

[21692] Capturing encrypted data today to decrypt once quantum computers are capable.

[21694] high

[21695] Statutory or rights-bearing; detriment is material and correction requires appeal or is not possible.

[21697] Human in the loop

[21698] A person who must act before an output takes effect.

[21700] Human on the loop

[21701] A person who monitors and can intervene in an otherwise automated process.

[21703] Human-agent system

[21704] The agent, the people who instruct and review it, and the controls between them, tested as one.

[21706] Information asset owner

[21707] The named person accountable for an information asset, its use, sharing and risks.

[21709] injected_instruction

[21710] Content in the case record attempts to redirect the agent.

[21712] Instruction block

[21713] The seven-part specification of an agent's behaviour: goal, context, sources, task, format, guardrails, output.

[21715] insufficient_confidence

[21716] The reviewer could not satisfy themselves either way and did not proceed.

[21718] Investment line

[21719] The full cost of adoption: visible, foundational, people and change, operational, and transition and exit.

[21721] Ironies of automation

[21722] Automation takes the easy, routine parts and leaves humans the hard residue while removing the routine practice through which people became competent at the hard parts. Structural root of the programme.

[21724] Kill switch

[21725] A control that stops an agent immediately and blocks further actions.

[21727] Lapsed

[21728] Had a stated end date which has now passed. Status after that date is unknown.

[21730] Least privilege

[21731] Granting only the minimum permissions needed for the shortest necessary time.

[21733] local_authority

[21734] Principal council or combined authority.

[21736] Lock-in

[21737] Dependency on a platform, model, connector or supplier that raises the cost or risk of leaving.

[21739] low

[21740] Recoverable before effect; no material detriment.

[21742] manager

[21743] Supervises a team performing any of the above.

[21745] Material AI assistance

[21746] AI involvement that a reasonable reader would want disclosed because it shaped the output.

[21748] Meaningful human involvement

[21749] Under the UK GDPR, a significant decision with no meaningful human involvement counts as solely automated and needs safeguards, including the right to contest it (Articles 22A to 22C, from 5 February 2026). The ICO's draft guidance says the person must have the authority, training and information to change the outcome, and actually consider it.

[21751] medium

[21752] Correctable through normal review; some detriment or delay.

[21754] missing_context

[21755] The output was reasonable on what it saw but omitted material the reviewer held.

[21757] Model Context Protocol (MCP)

[21758] An open standard that lets an AI client call tools and read resources on an outside system through one interface.

[21760] Model version churn

[21761] Silent model upgrade resets the error profile human trust calibration was built against.

[21763] Model-dependent finding

[21764] Finding about a specific model's output quality at a point in time; short half-life; re-verify before citing.

[21766] modify

[21767] Used after alteration.

[21769] Monoculture / correlated error

[21770] A few frontier models underpin most deployment so errors correlate across services.

[21772] Moral crumple zone

[21773] A human positioned as the responsible party for a system they could not realistically have controlled; liability absorption rather than accountability.

[21775] Neurodiverse (preferred) vs neurodivergent

[21776] The preferred term in this portal is "neurodiverse", used throughout the Inclusive use section.

[21778] nhs

[21779] NHS body or integrated care system.

[21781] none

[21782] Standard presentation.

[21784] Not located

[21785] The cited item could not be found to exist at all.

[21787] Novice pipeline

[21788] The supply of experienced people to do oversight, threatened by removal of entry-level roles whose routine work functioned as practice.

[21790] Orphaned agent

[21791] An agent still in use whose owner has moved on — the most common governance failure in a growing estate.

[21793] other_public_body

[21794] Any other public sector organisation.

[21796] Out-of-the-loop performance

[21797] Inability to re-acquire situational awareness fast enough when the system hands back Remedy: Handback design; keeping the human's mental model warm.

[21799] out_of_scope

[21800] The output addressed something outside the agent's approved scope. Also a drift signal.

[21802] Oversharing

[21803] Content reachable by more people than intended, usually through accumulated permission drift.

[21805] Oversight Assurance Layer

[21806] Shared platform component: schema, SDK, prior-capture widget, canary service, baseline scheduler, privacy-enforcing aggregation, currency ledger, conformance suite.

[21808] plausible_fabrication

[21809] A confident, well-formed output with no basis in the source material.

[21811] Plugin

[21812] A packaged custom action, such as an MCP or API plugin, that lets an agent read or change data in another system.

[21814] policy_misapplication

[21815] The output applied the wrong rule, threshold or guidance.

[21817] Positional

[21818] Who holds a role, what is in force, what has been published. Review quarterly.

[21820] PQC

[21821] Post-quantum cryptography — algorithms resistant to quantum attack.

[21823] Predict-then-reveal

[21824] User records provisional judgement (decision, confidence, one-line rationale) before agent output is displayed. Keystone pattern.

[21826] predict_then_reveal

[21827] The reviewer's provisional judgement was captured before the output was shown.

[21829] Preview

[21830] A feature released before general availability. Terms, controls and data handling may differ.

[21832] Process ossification

[21833] Agents encode current process; changing it means re-engineering agents, so process stops evolving.

[21835] Prohibited fields

[21836] Never present in an oversight event: user_id, staff_id, employee_id, staff_number, person_id, username, email, name, line_manager, ip_address, device_id. These must never appear in an oversight event, at any tier. The privacy contract is what makes the regime credible to staff and to unions; it is enforced in the schema, in the aggregator and in the analyser, not merely stated here.

[21838] Promotion gate

[21839] The checkpoint between personal, team, departmental, operational and cross-government scope.

[21841] Prompt injection

[21842] Untrusted content that manipulates a model into unintended actions.

[21844] Proportionality

[21845] Control matched to risk, autonomy, data sensitivity, decision influence and public effect.

[21847] Provenance

[21848] The verifiable record of where content, data or code came from and how it changed.

[21850] Provenance rot

[21851] Case records increasingly contain agent-generated text that future agents retrieve as evidence; record ceases to be an independent source.

[21853] reason_required

[21854] Approval required a structured reason.

[21856] Reasoned-disagreement sampling

[21857] Sample cases for independent human reasoning; grade quality of reasoning on both sides; never treat divergence as error. Replaces unaided-baseline sampling.

[21859] recommend

[21860] The output informs a decision that a person then makes about someone.

[21862] Recoverability

[21863] TBS Canada principle: pause/stop/return-to-safe-state by design; actions logged in a system the agent cannot alter; fail safely.

[21865] Register

[21866] The eighteen-field record every agent needs, held by the owning organisation, not by this guide.

[21868] reject

[21869] Not used; the reviewer produced their own outcome.

[21871] Residual risk

[21872] What remains after controls are applied — stated, owned and accepted rather than assumed away.

[21874] Responsibility diffusion

[21875] Accountability becomes hard across sub-agents, tool calls and cross-departmental service composition.

[21877] review

[21878] Proposed additions go to the vocabulary owner with a definition, a worked example, and a statement of why an existing code does not fit.

[21880] reviewer

[21881] Second-line check on another person's or system's output.

[21883] Scheme of delegation

[21884] Government's existing model of delegated authority with limits, thresholds, named accountable officers and withdrawal; agents should sit inside it.

[21886] Scissor (volume vs capability)

[21887] Volume requiring oversight rises with adoption while capability to oversee falls with the same adoption; reinforcing loop overload→skimming→atrophy.

[21889] scope_overstep

[21890] The agent proposes an action outside its permitted scope.

[21892] senior_caseworker

[21893] Handles complex or escalated cases.

[21895] Seniority-biased technological change

[21896] Harvard working-paper term for entry-level hiring falling at generative-AI-adopting firms.

[21898] Shadow AI

[21899] Unregistered tools in operational use: unknown ownership, cost and risk. Maturity level zero.

[21901] Skill

[21902] A packaged, versioned capability an assistant or agent can invoke, with defined inputs and limits.

[21904] Skill atrophy

[21905] Degradation of the knowledge and practised judgement that oversight roles depend on, caused by sustained offloading of the underlying task. (Adopted from TBS Canada.)

[21907] Sophistication index

[21908] The prototype quality score across grounding, evaluation, guardrails, observability and support.

[21910] Source tiering

[21911] Ranking sources by authority so conflicts resolve predictably.

[21913] stability

[21914] Codes are additive. A code is never removed or repurposed; superseded codes are marked deprecated with a successor.

[21916] stale_data

[21917] The output relies on superseded information.

[21919] Structural

[21920] An argument, framework or finding about how things work. Review annually.

[21922] Structural finding

[21923] Human-factors/organisational finding about people and institutions; durable across model versions.

[21925] Subprocessor

[21926] A third party that processes data on behalf of the supplier, such as a model provider.

[21928] Substitutive use

[21929] AI use that replaces a judgement the practitioner would otherwise exercise (e.g. assessing whether an argument holds, deciding a course of action, interpreting data, summarising a policy paper one would otherwise have read). Carries the same oversight risk regardless of neurotype.

[21931] Superseded

[21932] Was correct when recorded; a later event has changed the position.

[21934] Supervisory control

[21935] Human-automation interaction concept; agency is a variable set per task and context on a levels-of-automation scale.

[21937] time_to_decision_ms

[21938] From presentation of the output to recording of the disposition. Excludes time before the item was opened.

[21940] tone_or_style

[21941] Presentation only; substance unchanged.

[21943] Unit economics

[21944] Cost and value per interaction: the figure that decides whether an agent earns its keep.

[21946] Unverified

[21947] No accessible primary or strong institutional source located across two independent passes. Not relied upon.

[21949] Verification state

[21950] Whether a claim is verified, verified in substance, unverified, superseded, lapsed or not located.

[21952] Verified

[21953] Source located; organisation, date and substance all confirmed.

[21955] Verified in substance

[21956] Claim is correct but the originally cited link, reference or date did not resolve.

[21958] Vigilance decrement

[21959] Sustained-attention performance falls sharply within the first half hour of monitoring Remedy: Queue design, shift length, task interleaving.

[21961] Volatile

[21962] Supplier rate cards, product availability, live counts. Verify at point of use; never cache.

## Frequently asked questions [21964]

[21967] Do I have to declare every use of AI?

[21969] No. Declare material assistance — where AI shaped the substance, structure, analysis or code of an output. Trivial uses such as spell-checking do not need a declaration, but your local policy may set a lower threshold.

[21971] Can AI approve my work?

[21973] No. AI can suggest, draft, check and explain. Approval is a human act by someone with the authority to make that decision. AI never grants authority a user does not already hold.

[21975] What if the AI cites a source that does not exist?

[21977] Treat it as an incident. Do not publish. Verify every citation against the original, log the failure in the drift and incident register, and check whether the same prompt pattern has been used elsewhere.

[21979] Is this a substitute for a DPIA, EQIA or security assurance?

[21981] No. This toolkit helps you prepare and evidence those assessments; it does not replace them or the professionals accountable for them.

[21983] Can I paste official-sensitive information into a general assistant?

[21985] Not unless the tool is explicitly approved for that classification and the data-handling terms have been assured. When in doubt, do not paste — ask your information asset owner.

[21987] How do I handle AI-generated code?

[21989] Treat it as untrusted third-party code: review it, test it, scan dependencies, record provenance and never merge without a human reviewer who understands it.

[21991] What accessibility duties apply to AI-generated content?

[21993] The same ones that apply to everything else. WCAG 2.2 AA, plain language, alternative formats and the accessibility statement duty all apply regardless of who or what drafted the content.

[21995] Who do I contact if something goes wrong?

[21997] Your service owner and the named AI assurance contact for your organisation. Report near-misses too — they are the cheapest form of learning.

# Authoritative guidance, standards and reusable intelligence

[Open this section on the publisher’s website](https://cyberdudeuk.github.io/ai-capability-governance/#knowledge)

The numbers in brackets identify elements in the ordered DOM inventory. This is a text projection of Em’s material.

## Authoritative guidance, standards and reusable intelligence [19916]

[19917] The corpus is organised as a knowledge graph linking laws, policies, standards, design guidance, security controls, skills, agents and evidence — so that a rule can always be traced to its source and its consequences.

## Guidance corpus [19921]

[19922] Index GOV.UK, GDS, CDDO, departmental, international standards, GitHub and engineering-lab sources with authority tiering, freshness checks and applicability metadata.

[19923] Browse the 69 indexed sources →

## Knowledge graph [19927]

[19928] Link services, repositories, datasets, APIs, controls, skills, agents, people, approvals, models, risks and evidence so impact analysis is a query, not a workshop.

[19929] See the metadata model →

## Executable guidance [19933]

[19934] Translate policy and standards into schemas, conformance packs, tests, scripts, checklists and prompt patterns that run in delivery pipelines.

[19935] See the conformance packs →

## Authority tiering — how conflicts are resolved [19937]

[19938] When two sources disagree, the lower tier number wins. Record the conflict and the resolution in the evidence pack.

[19941] Source authority tiers used across the corpus

[19944] Tier

[19945] Source type

[19946] Examples

[19947] Treatment

[19950] 0

[19952] Law and statutory instruments

[19953] Equality Act 2010, DPA 2018, Accessibility Regulations 2018

[19954] Binding. Non-compliance is not a risk to accept — escalate.

[19956] 1

[19958] Mandated standards and cross-government policy

[19959] Service Standard, Technology Code of Practice, Secure by Design, WCAG 2.2, ATRS

[19960] Comply or record a formal, time-boxed exception with an owner.

[19962] 2

[19964] Recognised international and professional standards

[19965] ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF, OWASP LLM Top 10

[19966] Adopt as good practice; justify divergence.

[19968] 3

[19970] Community, vendor and research material

[19971] Blogs, model cards, toolkits, preprints

[19972] Useful signal. Never the sole basis for a control or a public claim.

## Freshness and drift controls [19973]

## Every indexed source carries [19976]

[19978] • Authority tier and issuing body

[19979] • Date checked and next check due

[19980] • Applicability (organisation, service type, data classification)

[19981] • Supersession chain and withdrawal status

[19982] • Linked controls, skills and conformance tests

## Drift triggers a review when [19984]

[19986] • A cited source is updated, withdrawn or superseded

[19987] • A model or its version changes materially

[19988] • A control fails in production or a conformance test breaks

[19989] • An incident, complaint or FOI request touches the artefact

[19990] • The scheduled review date passes without confirmation

# Assure and govern

[Open this section on the publisher’s website](https://cyberdudeuk.github.io/ai-capability-governance/#part-assure-and-govern)

The numbers in brackets identify elements in the ordered DOM inventory. This is a text projection of Em’s material.

[4928] Part 4 of 12 · 13 chapters

## Assure and govern [4929]

[4938] Responsible AI · govern and assure

## One control plane for any tool, model or agent [4939]

[4940] Consistent principles, proportionate assurance and reusable components. Evidence and transparency records sit with the controls because they are how each control is shown to work.

## Principles and risk [4946]

[4947] Capability-based classification sets the assurance depth.

## Information and data [4951]

[4952] Readiness, metadata, indexing, provenance and retention.

## Security and privacy [4956]

[4957] Threat model, DPIA, transfers, subprocessors and DLP.

## Human oversight [4961]

[4962] Reviewer competence, evidence access, override and stop.

## Accessibility and inclusion [4966]

[4967] Accessibility of AI, AI for accessibility, alternatives and adjustments.

## Cost and FinOps [4971]

[4972] User-visible cost, caps, alerts, budget owners and value criteria.

## Sustainability [4976]

[4977] Supplier evidence, usage indicators and proportionate use.

## Transparency and records [4981]

[4982] AI involvement statements, labelling and audit evidence.

## Monitoring and assurance [4986]

[4987] Control effectiveness, incidents and reviews.

## Change and lifecycle [4991]

[4992] Change watchlist, reassessment triggers and retirement.

## Who owns what [4993]

[4999] Role

[5000] Accountable for

[5003] Senior responsible owner

[5004] Risk acceptance, sponsorship and the decision to proceed or stop.

[5006] Service owner

[5007] Day-to-day operation, monitoring, support and retirement.

[5009] Technical owner

[5010] Configuration, identity, permissions, release and change.

[5012] Commercial owner

[5013] Contract, licences, consumption, supplier commitments and exit.

[5015] Assurance owner

[5016] Assessments, evidence, exceptions and reviews.

[5018] Budget owner

[5019] Caps, alerts and spend against value evidence.

[5021] Agent, prompt or skill owner

[5022] Version, tests, approved users and withdrawal.

## Exceptions and the shadow AI route [5025]

[5026] Unmanaged external use falls when asking for an approved alternative is quicker than working around the rules.

[5028] Search your organisation's catalogue for an approved alternative.

[5029] If none fits, request one through a use case with the reason it is needed.

[5030] Get an interim decision within an agreed time, with conditions.

[5031] Record the exception in the decision register with an expiry date.

[5032] Review at expiry: approve, restrict or close.

## Communication authenticity [5034]

[5035] Keep clear labels on AI-sent messages and disclose material AI involvement. Removing a label is prohibited where transparency is required.

## Evidence and transparency records [5036]

## AI involvement statements [5039]

[5040] What AI did in producing a document, decision or message.

## Source records [5042]

[5043] The sources an output drew on, so a reader can check them.

## Human verification [5045]

[5046] Who checked the output, against what, and when.

## Decision-support records [5048]

[5049] How AI informed a decision and who made it.

## Code records [5051]

[5052] Provenance and review of AI-generated code.

## Agent action logs [5054]

[5055] What an agent did, when and why.

## Audit evidence [5057]

[5058] Configuration, approvals and test results for assurance.

## Evidence grades for product and supplier claims [5059]

[5060] These sit alongside the guide's own conventions (verified, interpretation, proposal, illustrative). They grade claims about products and suppliers, many of which come from community calls.

## Verified [5063]

[5064] Confirmed against authoritative supplier documentation or a live configuration.

## Corroborated [5066]

[5067] Reported by more than one independent source or session.

## Reported [5069]

[5070] Raised in a community call or channel. Not yet confirmed.

## Proposed [5072]

[5073] A design recommendation in this portal, not a finding.

## Unresolved [5075]

[5076] An open question. Do not rely on it until answered.

[5077] Back to the contents · Suggest a correction (opens GitHub)

[5089] Assure and govern · data and information governance

## AI governance is data governance with actions attached [5090]

[5091] Whatever an AI tool can reach, it can surface, summarise and act on. Data and information governance sets what it should reach, and treats what it produces as records.

[5097] Ownership and accountability Every source has an information asset owner; the senior information risk owner accepts residual risk.

[5102] Classification and handling Classification travels with content into prompts, indexes and outputs.

[5107] Data protection UK GDPR lawful basis, DPIA, transfers, rights and service-level privacy notices.

[5112] Quality and authority Grounding sources are authoritative, current and fit for the decision they inform.

[5117] Metadata and discoverability Titles, filenames and metadata can surface through AI. Discovery is not access.

[5122] Records and retention Prompts, outputs, transcripts and agent logs are records with retention rules.

[5127] Access and permissions Least privilege, oversharing clean-up, delegated and shared contexts tested.

[5132] Sharing and reuse Data-sharing agreements, data boundaries and trusted reuse such as data matchmaking.

## Data controls at each lifecycle stage [5134]

[5140] Stage

[5141] Data and information control

[5142] Where it is recorded

[5145] 1 Discover

[5146] Identify the information assets involved and their owners

[5147] T1 Opportunity Brief

[5149] 2 Check

[5150] Reuse existing datasets, catalogues and indexes before creating new ones

[5151] T2 Duplication Check

[5153] 3 Classify

[5154] Classification, personal data and special category data

[5155] T3 Classification

[5157] 4 Assess

[5158] DPIA, lawful basis, transfers and subprocessors, data quality and authority

[5159] T4 Data Readiness · T5 Supplier

[5161] 5 Design

[5162] Metadata, index scope, permissions, connectors and retention rules

[5163] T7 Agent Design Record · data-source register

[5165] 6 Pilot

[5166] Minimisation, test data, consent and privacy notices

[5167] T8 Pilot Plan

[5169] 10 Operate

[5170] Access reviews, DLP, records of AI outputs and agent logs

[5171] Monitoring and assurance record

[5173] 11 Reassess

[5174] New sources, connectors or locations trigger review

[5175] T11 Change-Impact Assessment

[5177] 12 Retire

[5178] Disposal, records transfer and revoked access

[5179] T12 Retirement Record

## What AI creates is information too [5180]

## Prompts and instructions [5183]

[5184] Retain where they shaped a decision or a published output; organisational prompts are versioned products.

## AI outputs [5186]

[5187] Treat as drafts until a person verifies them; keep the verified version with an AI involvement statement.

## Transcripts and recordings [5189]

[5190] Consent notice, retention period and deletion route set before recording starts.

## Agent action logs [5192]

[5193] Keep for audit and incident review; owner can read them.

## Indexes and embeddings [5195]

[5196] Derived copies of source data; inherit the source classification and retention.

## Evaluation data [5198]

[5199] Test sets and results are evidence for the decision record.

## Frameworks this aligns with [5202]

[5203] Data Ethics Framework ↗ (opens an external website) UK government framework for using data responsibly in policy and services.

[5206] Government Data Quality Framework ↗ (opens an external website) Principles and practices for assessing and improving data quality.

[5209] ICO guidance on AI and data protection ↗ (opens an external website) How UK GDPR applies to AI, including fairness, transparency and DPIAs.

[5212] Northern Ireland draft AI Strategy ↗ (opens an external website) Data governance is one of the eight proposed principles.

[5215] Scotland’s AI Strategy 2026–2031 ↗ (opens an external website) Data framed as a public asset, with a data matchmaking pilot.

## Seen in practice [5219]

[5220] Kingston Council ran a DPIA on data flows, storage and access before going live with AI note-taking, and updated its privacy notice. Hartlepool publishes a service-level privacy notice for the same kind of tool. Belfast City Council put data and AI governance under one Data & Analytics Board.

[5221] Back to the contents · Suggest a correction (opens GitHub)

[5233] Architecture of trust

## Governing AI agents as digital workers [5234]

[5235] A continuous cycle that governs AI agents as digital workers to deliver trusted public services and outcomes. The agent at the centre is purpose driven, accountable, supervised, transparent, secure and ethical. Trust at every step: right agent, right authority, right outcome.

## Know the agent [5241]

[5243] Define purpose and role

[5244] Register and record

[5245] Assign owners

## Capability [5248]

## What it can do [5249]

[5251] Define capabilities

[5252] Tools, data, knowledge

[5253] Evaluate and test

## Authority [5256]

## What it is allowed to do [5257]

[5259] Set boundaries

[5260] Permissions & limits

[5261] Approval thresholds

## Policy & guardrails [5264]

## How it must operate [5265]

[5267] Policies & rules

[5268] Ethics & responsible AI

[5269] Guardrails & constraints

## Approval [5272]

## Authorise to operate [5273]

[5275] Risk assessment

[6271] Human oversight · principles

## The human directs; AI is in the loop [6272]

[6273] Ten principles for keeping people in charge of AI-assisted work: oversight is a competence to build and measure, not a box to tick. From the Responsible AI and Data Use (RAIDU) work, merged into this playbook on 22 November 2026. Each item keeps its evidence grade: Proposed items are design proposals for review, not policy or established practice.

## P1 The human directs; AI is in the loop [6278]

[6279] Accountability

[6281] The person is always in the director position. AI works inside a scope the person sets, and is given agency only if, when and where it is warranted. Oversight competence means setting good bounds, reading the evidence that they are wrong, and withdrawing agency without the service collapsing.

[6282] Evidence grade: Proposed

## P2 Control intensity follows consequence [6284]

[6285] Proportionality

[6287] Classify every deployment as assist, recommend or determine before choosing controls. The productivity evidence comes from drafting, summarising and analysis; none of it comes from determining anything about a person. Drafting-grade controls on determination is the real risk; determination-grade controls on drafting forfeits real value.

[6288] Evidence grade: Proposed

## P3 Attention is a budget, not a tax [6290]

[6291] Proportionality

[6293] Most interactions should carry no friction. High-consequence, high-uncertainty and novel cases get the full set. The first control is to reduce what reaches a person at all: triage, confidence-gating and risk-proportionate friction. You cannot train your way out of a capacity problem.

[6294] Evidence grade: Proposed

## P4 Measure oversight; never assume it [6296]

[6297] Assurance

[6299] Every UK instrument makes human oversight the primary safeguard and none checks whether it still works. Behavioural signals lead; self-report, attestation and training completion do not count as evidence.

[6300] Evidence grade: Proposed

## P5 Measure the system, never the person [6302]

[6303] Privacy and trust

[6305] Oversight measurement is aggregate and non-attributable, enforced in code with minimum cohort sizes. Individual-level oversight measurement is ruled out in any form. Unions are design partners before build, on a just-culture basis.

[6306] Evidence grade: Proposed

## P6 Assured oversight unlocks autonomy [6308]

[6309] Delivery

[6311] Evidence of maintained oversight is what lets a team take the human out of more loops safely. Positioned as a brake it will be routed around; positioned as the route to more autonomy, delivery teams will ask for it.

[6312] Evidence grade: Proposed

## P7 Verify, never fabricate [6314]

[6315] Integrity

[6317] No figure, citation, claim or capability is asserted unless it can be reproduced from a source or the data. What cannot be reproduced is labelled modelled, estimated or unconfirmed on the face of the artefact. Treat any AI-produced draft as hypotheses.

[6318] Evidence grade: Proposed

## P8 Compensating is not substituting [6320]

[6321] Inclusion

[6323] Using AI to get past a stable barrier (structuring a draft, checking tone, holding many things in mind) is assistive technology. Using it to replace a judgement you could form yourself is where skill atrophy lives. A blanket rule to keep using skills unaided would be an accessibility regression.

[6324] Evidence grade: Proposed

## P9 Disclose AI assistance at the right level [6326]

[6327] Transparency

[6329] Classify AI-assisted work by audience (internal, peer co-design, external) and apply the matching disclosure. The human keeps the framework, structure, final selection and original contributions; AI output is raw material that is reviewed, accepted, rejected and shaped.

[6330] Evidence grade: Proposed

## P10 Evidence-led, with a stated exit [6332]

[6333] Integrity

[6335] If longitudinal research finds no material oversight decay in administrative settings, the currency regime scales back to sampling only. Stating in advance what would change our mind is what keeps the programme evidence-led.

[6336] Evidence grade: Proposed

## Treat AI output as a draft to check, not a source [7049]

[7050] Practices for checking AI-assisted research, analysis and artefacts before they are relied on, and failure patterns seen in public sector work. From the Responsible AI and Data Use (RAIDU) work, merged into this playbook on 22 November 2026. Each item keeps its evidence grade: Proposed items are design proposals for review, not policy or established practice.

## Evidence handling [7053]

[7055] Treat an AI-produced research draft as hypotheses only. An AI-produced research draft was treated as a source of hypotheses only. None of its assertions was carried forward unchecked. Each source in that draft was located independently, and the result of every check was recorded, including failures.

[7057] Keep unverifiable claims, marked. Claims that could not be substantiated were kept and marked. Deleting them would remove the evidence of the checking.

[7059] Provenance travels with each claim. The unit here is the claim, not the document. In a portal people land on one assertion without meeting the caveats that make it safe to use, so the provenance travels with each claim.

[7061] Label researcher interpretation. Interpretations are labelled, never presented as findings (enforced by CHK-004).

[7063] Prefer counterfactual evaluations. The comparison against which a benefit is measured, typically a group not using the tool. An evaluation without one cannot separate the tool's effect from everything else. The two evaluations with a comparison or randomised design, DWP and HMRC, report lower figures than those without. Expect that pattern to hold elsewhere.

[7065] Treat supplier evidence as interested-party. Supplier — treated as interested-party evidence; verified independently wherever possible.

[7067] Grounding quality. Supplying an AI system with specific approved source material so its output is based on that material. Grounding quality is a function of source quality and currency.

[7069] Read live rate cards at point of use. Supplier terms. Read the live rate card at the point of building any business case; do not quote these figures from the portal.

[7071] Ask for realised-outcome evidence rather than inferring it. The NHS England rollout date has arrived, so ask NHS England for realised-outcome evidence rather than inferring it.

## Security and privacy [7073]

[7075] Use the DPIA as a design tool from day one. Embed DPIA as a design tool at the start of every build; non-digital fallback routes; test with affected groups; document Equality Act/PSED compliance by default.

## Delivery [7077]

[7079] Due diligence on AI-assisted development. Due diligence on AI-assisted development methodology should cover GDS delivery alignment, AI assistance scope, IPR and Crown copyright, spend assurance (GDS spend controls were withdrawn on 1 April 2026 and replaced by the Digital Assurance Playbook), data handling and ethical AI use.

## Self-check pattern [7081]

[7083] Every case cites at least one source, and every source exists. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7085] Every figure carries a status label and a resolvable source. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7087] Every case has a known mechanism and every mapped control resolves. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7089] Dates are valid year-month values. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7091] Case and source identifiers are unique. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7093] No attributed death count appears on the face of any case. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7095] Anchor case states the causation limit before any consequence claim. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7097] Figures add up: the fines total is computed, not typed. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7099] Anything not re-verified this release is listed as carried, not shown as fact. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7101] Sources are fresh (checked within 90 days of viewing). A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7103] Coverage spans sectors and all four UK nations. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7105] Every challenge states what the objection gets right and the limit of the claim. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7107] Displayed money totals stay within 0.5% of the computed figure. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7109] Vendor documentation is labelled supplier evidence, and only vendor sources carry that label. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7111] Every connection states the tie and the action, and every link is a full https address. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7113] Counts written into the text match the data. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7115] Citations of the standard do not depend on the retiring co-cddo organisation. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7117] Every post referenced in the seam, triad and resolution register exists in the join-up map. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7119] The resolution register covers every mechanism and every case, and cites only real cases. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7121] Every computed placeholder in the text has a value. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7123] Every case has a DAM Policy assessment, and each case's rules agree with each rule's cases. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7125] Proposed return rules use the workspace's own grammar and every in-scope case is answered by one. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

[7127] verified / reported / estimate / supplier evidence / author's account; sums of estimates are not audited totals; vendor docs labelled supplier evidence only (K14).. A check that runs on the artefact itself. It exists because of the defect shown.

## Failure patterns to recognise [7129]

## The Hidden Tab Pattern [7132]

[7133] Responsible data use

[7135] Files and messages leave organisations carrying more personal data than the sender can see or intended to send; the sensitivity/handling label sits in a register or catalogue entry that stays behind and does not travel with the file to the point of release, so nothing at the boundary can read it.

[7136] Case: MOD (UK Special Forces HQ), February 2022: a spreadsheet believed to hold about 150 Afghan relocation applicants carried, invisibly, details of about 18,700. Twin case: PSNI, August 2023, a second tab on an FOI answer exposed every officer (ICO fine £750,000).

## Synthetic data presented as real [7138]

[7139] Verifying AI-assisted work

[7141] An AI assistant described synthetic events as real output, and an early build of the oversight instrument repeated it. Anything generated must be labelled on its face.

[7142] Case: Found and corrected during review, 2026.

## Hand-typed figures drift from the data [7144]

[7145] Verifying AI-assisted work

[7147] A figure typed rather than computed drifts from the data it claims to summarise. Compute totals; never type them.

[7148] Case: A figure typed into an appraisal differed materially from the figure computed from its data; caught by a check that recomputes totals.

# Decide and prioritise

[Open this section on the publisher’s website](https://cyberdudeuk.github.io/ai-capability-governance/#part-decide-and-prioritise)

The numbers in brackets identify elements in the ordered DOM inventory. This is a text projection of Em’s material.

[2114] Part 2 of 12 · 6 chapters

## Decide and prioritise [2115]

[2124] The evidence

## Same product. Four UK evaluations. Four answers. [2125]

[2126] What varies is method, not the tool. Uncontrolled self-report gives the highest figures; comparison-group econometrics gives mid-range; counterfactual-free evaluation of a short pilot gives the lowest. Role mix is the second driver.

[2130] 26

[2131] minutes / day

## Cross-government, GDS [2132]

[2133] 20,000 staff, self-reported

[2135] 60

[2136] minutes / week

[2138] 3,000 licences

[2143] 3,549 staff, econometric

[2145] 0

[2146] robust evidence

## DBT, no counterfactual [2147]

[2148] 1,000 licences

[2149] Never average these numbers. The spread is evidence about evaluation design. Sources: GDS findings report (Jun 2025); HMRC phase 3; DWP evaluation (Jan 2026); DBT evaluation (Aug 2025).

## Four things block the move to governed scale [2151]

## Unremediated permissions [2154]

[2155] AI surfaces what a user may already reach. Permission drift becomes an incident on day one.

[2156] Makes scaling UNSAFE

## No agent inventory [2158]

[2159] The transparency standard records algorithmic tools. It is not an operational register of agents.

[2160] Makes scaling UNGOVERNABLE

## Unpredictable consumption cost [2162]

[2163] Credits are billed per feature, not per conversation. A builder's design choice sets a budget holder's cost.

[2164] Makes scaling UNBUDGETABLE

## Unfunded human effort [2166]

[2167] Workflow redesign, local support and output verification happen but rarely appear as funded lines.

[2168] Makes scaling UNSUSTAINABLE

## Activity is running ahead of visibility [2169]

[2170] Between deployment and disclosure sits a gap no current UK instrument closes. The ATRS is a transparency mechanism, not an inventory: it does not capture team-shared agents, orphaned agents, data-source approval, consumption cost or retirement.

## Coding agents: two findings, both real [2190]

[2191] A finding about where to deploy, not whether.

## 1 hr [2194]

[2196] saved per day — GDS cross-government trial, 50 organisations

[2197] 72% said good value; 58% would not return to working without it

## 19% [2202]

[2204] slower — METR randomised trial: experienced developers, mature code

[2205] 20% felt faster — the same developers, in the same trial

[2208] Benefit is largest on well-scoped, greenfield and boilerplate work; smallest or negative on mature, complex codebases. Developer self-assessment is unreliable in both directions. Join the AI Engineering Lab (OCTO, GDS) before procuring independently — the evidence you generate is reusable.

## What the enthusiastic version leaves out [2210]

[2211] Contrary evidence, recorded deliberately.

## 17% [2214]

[2216] of cross-government trial users noticed no clear time savings (GDS, Jun 2025)

## 7% [2219]

[2221] of Australian participants reported the tool added time (DTA, Oct 2024)

## 61% [2224]

[2226] of Australian managers could not confidently identify AI outputs (DTA, Oct 2024)

## 72% [2229]

[2231] of councils were not ready on workforce skills and expertise (LGA, Jun 2025)

[2232] Canada names a further risk no UK instrument addresses: skill atrophy and automation drift. Skill maintenance is a prerequisite for meaningful human oversight, not an optional extra (TBS Canada, May 2026).

## A caution on AI-produced research [2234]

[2235] Twenty sources in one AI research draft. What checking found:

[2238] 7

[2239] verified precisely

[2241] 6

[2242] verified in substance

[2244] 4

[2245] not verified as cited

[2247] 1

[2248] could not be located

[2249] None of the unverifiable entries was obvious: each was correctly formatted, plausibly dated, attributed to a real institution. Treat AI-produced research as a hypothesis-generating artefact, never an evidence base — and keep the verification log with the output.

## Evidence labels used across this app [2250]

[2253] Verified fact — supported by official, regulatory, audit or primary sources

[2256] Organisation-reported — reported by the organisation itself, not independently measured

[2259] Supplier claim — authoritative for product terms; interested-party evidence for value

[2262] Interpretation — analytical judgement drawn from cited evidence

[2265] Recommendation — action proposed, not established practice

[2268] Unresolved — evidence incomplete, conflicting or arrangement-specific

## Where AI creates value across government and public services [2283]

[2284] Eighteen categories, from productivity tools to enterprise agents — supporting people, processes and public outcomes. Use AI and agents responsibly to enhance the work of public servants and improve outcomes for citizens.

[2288] 1. Knowledge retrieval & insight Find, summarise and synthesise information from trusted sources

[2291] 2. Content & correspondence Draft, edit and refine high-quality content and communications

[2294] 3. Contact centres & helpdesks Support staff and citizens with accurate, consistent responses

[2297] 4. Casework & service operations Streamline case handling, triage and workflow automation

[2300] 5. Citizen services & engagement Deliver simpler, faster and more accessible services

[2303] 6. Meetings & collaboration Capture, summarise and turn meetings into actions and outcomes

[2306] 7. Data analysis & reporting Analyse data, create summaries and produce management information

[2309] 8. Software engineering & IT operations Accelerate development, testing and secure operations

[2312] 9. HR & people management Improve people processes and the employee experience

[2315] 10. Finance & procurement Enhance financial planning, analysis and supplier management

[2318] 11. Education, training & skills Personalise learning and improve knowledge retention

[2321] 12. Programme & project management Plan, track and report with intelligent support

[2324] 13. Health & care Support clinical and administrative workflows safely and securely

[2327] 14. Policing, justice & public safety Improve investigations, evidence handling and public protection

[2330] 15. Regulatory & compliance Monitor compliance and produce regulatory outputs

## Cross-cutting capabilities — enablers for all use cases [2343]

[2344] Secure access to trusted data & knowledge AI agents & orchestration (autonomy with oversight) Human oversight & accountability Privacy, security & data protection Quality assurance & model evaluation Observability, monitoring & auditability Integration with systems & workflows Change management & adoption FinOps & cost management

## Foundational enablers [2355]

[2356] Data quality & governance Information management Access management Standards & interoperability Skills & culture Ethics & responsible AI

## The use-case evidence card [2363]

[2364] A consistent way to describe, evaluate and share AI use-case evidence: what the capability does, who it helps, how it works, the value it delivers, and the evidence that supports it. Evidence first. Value always. Capture consistently, share openly, decide confidently.

[2367] 1. Basic information Use case name · Short description · Unique ID · Date created · Last updated · Author / owner

[2370] 2. Problem & purpose Problem / opportunity · Purpose & objectives · Success criteria

[2373] 3. Users & context Primary user groups · Who benefits · Operating context / environment · Geography / organisation

[2376] 4. Solution & capability AI capability / agent type · Key features / functions · How it works (high level) · Human oversight points

[2379] 5. Data & information Key data sources · Type of data · Data sensitivity · Information governance

[2382] 6. Implementation & integration Platform / technology · Systems / tools integrated · Deployment model · Date went live / expected · Resource requirements

[2385] 7. Outcomes & value Quantitative outcomes (measured) · Qualitative outcomes (observed) · Value delivered (how & for whom)

[2388] 8. Costs & financials Cost model (licence, usage, etc.) · Estimated / actual cost · Cost per user / transaction · Ongoing cost considerations · Funding source / owner

[2391] 9. Risks & assurance Key risks · Mitigations in place · Assurance / evaluation approach

[2394] 10. Evidence & validation Evidence summary · Evidence sources · What evidence is available (performance results, user feedback, evaluation report, audit / review, other)

[2397] 11. Limitations & lessons Known limitations / constraints · Lessons learned / recommendations

[2400] 12. Transferability & reuse Potential for reuse (high / medium / low) · Reusable artefacts available · Transferability notes

[2403] 13. Lifecycle & review Lifecycle stage (ideation, pilot, live, scaled, retired) · Review frequency · Next review date · Sunset / retirement plan

## Evidence strength [2407]

[2409] Strong — Independently validated

[2411] Medium — Reported results with some validation

[2413] Emerging — Pilot / early indications

[2415] Weak — Unverified claims

[2417] Unknown — Insufficient evidence

## Evidence status [2420]

[2421] Live / in use Pilot / trial Planned Retired / stopped Unknown

## Worked, failed and unproven [2427]

[2428] Sharing the full picture — successes, failures and emerging ideas — so we learn faster and build smarter. Transparent evidence helps the public sector avoid repeating mistakes and scale what works. The cases below are illustrative.

[2431] Worked — repeatable success

## Case: ACAS 'Haste' helpline knowledge assistant [2433]

## What worked [2435]

[2437] Grounded in authoritative, approved and consistent formats

[2445] Improved accuracy and consistency

## What went wrong [2453]

## Classify first, then answer only what your tier needs [2758]

[2759] As AI can see more, do more and act more independently, the assurance required rises. Criticality & gates scores the service impact; this chapter sets the route from what the AI itself can do.

## Where you are, and how much control that needs [3296]

[3297] Two illustrative frameworks from the capability report: a seven-stage maturity model for organisations, and six assurance tiers for agents. Neither scores named organisations; both are diagnostic tools to calibrate against evidence. Over-control halts adoption; under-control creates unmanaged exposure.

## The seven-stage maturity model [3299]

[3301] Observable evidence at stage 2

[3302] Bounded pilots; named sponsors; temporary funding; largely self-reported benefit evidence.

## Evidence to collect before claiming progression [3303]

[3304] Named owners, repeatable gates, measured outcomes — not licensed tools.

## Leadership & service ownership [3308]

[3310] Named accountable owners, clear outcomes, risk appetite and decision records.

## People & workforce [3313]

[3315] Role-based training, protected learning time, inclusive adoption measures, staff consultation.

## Technology & agents [3318]

## Data & information [3323]

[3325] Authoritative sources, metadata, permissions remediation, retention, provenance.

## Security & assurance [3328]

[3330] Threat model, DPIA where required, evaluation evidence, incident route, audit logs.

## Commercial & supplier [3333]

[3335] Licensing clarity, usage data, audit rights, exit, substitution, support terms.

## Finance & FinOps [3338]

[3340] Forecasts, showback, anomaly alerts, unit economics, value attribution.

## Community learning [3343]

[3345] Reusable artefacts, supersession, contribution workflow, evidence of reuse.

## Six agent assurance tiers — controls scale with autonomy [3346]

[3347] Bounded autonomy and recoverability adopted from Government of Canada agentic-AI guidance (May 2026).

[3352] Personal assistant Drafting, summarisation and retrieval for one accountable user

[3355] Acceptable-use policy, permissions hygiene, human verification, retention and transparency guidance.

[3360] Personal or team agent Bounded knowledge and repeatable team tasks

[3363] Registered owner, approved sources, test prompts, sharing gate, usage telemetry.

[3368] Departmental reusable agent Multiple teams or a repeatable departmental process

[3371] Business, technical, information, risk and support owners; service level; change control; retirement plan.

[3376] Operational agent Acts on records, workflows or line-of-business systems

[3379] Distinct identity, least privilege, action logging, rollback, incident response, continuous monitoring.

[3384] Citizen-impacting agent Influences access, rights, safety, services or public communication

[3387] Impact assessment, legal basis, accessibility and equality assessment, transparency, redress, independent assurance.

[3392] Autonomous / multi-agent Delegated goals, tools, sub-agents or long-running actions

[3395] Sandboxing, constrained authority, short-lived credentials, kill switch, behavioural monitoring, dependency mapping.

## Tier finder — two questions set the tier at intake [3397]

[3398] What may this agent do without asking, and what can be undone when it goes wrong?

## Deploy for real [15362]

## Fifty-four public services, placed [15372]

[15373] The highest-volume services across UK central government, local government and the NHS, placed on two axes that decide almost everything else: how much of it there is, and what happens when it is wrong. Select a quadrant or a factor to filter. Open any service to load it into the generator.

## How to read this, and how not to [15389]

[15390] Volume bands come from published transaction data; criticality and the factor tags are an assessment of consequence, not a classification you can cite. The value is not the placement — it is that placing a service forces a conversation about consequence that a business case usually skips. [15465] Tool over-permission High
